raw.assessment: The incumbent plausibly works well for stable courses: unchanged-assignment files had seven-minute median handling, below the 12-minute target. Overall course-set accuracy was 80%, below 95%; assignment changes and renames characterize all eight affected exports but do not establish causation. Current-assignment semantics suggest a historical-selection mismatch. Fast execution and long replacement waits suggest a separate delay, without measuring active handling. A concrete limit is D1-O4: zero observed cross-center rows excludes the recently split course and cannot establish isolation there. Coordinator spreadsheet actions remain unobserved.

openings.claim: Selecting courses through current assignments or mutable names may misrepresent the requested week's course set; stable identity with week-relevant membership may reduce these errors.
openings.delta: Test temporal selection semantics before changing Sunday scheduling or increasing execution capacity.
openings.prediction: With intended membership fixed, an assignment or name change alters incumbent selection incorrectly; week-relevant identity selection retains the intended set. Course splits may expose an additional lineage rule.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging data, compare unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split-course fixtures against explicit weekly expectations. Include another center and concurrent attendance entry. Compare existing and candidate selectors while retaining the documented CSV. Bound investigation and any change to six engineer-days and existing hosting; do not assume a historical repair is feasible.
assumptions: Historical assignment and course identity data may be available; availability and implementation cost are unverified.
Expected treatment of split courses must be specified by coordinators.

openings.claim: Does excess active handling primarily occur in course reconciliation, CSV importing, or requesting replacements?
openings.delta: Separate active effort from replacement waiting to identify which change can meet the handling-time target.
openings.prediction: A reconciliation explanation predicts greater checking/correction time for changed-course fixtures; an import explanation predicts substantial importing time even for correct, stable-course files.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two short sessions with fabricated stable and changed-course exports, counterbalancing order. Time checking, correcting, downloading, importing and replacement requests separately; record waiting separately. Keep materials in authorized workspaces and fit both probes within the shared budget.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate ordinary work; session results require confirmation across the next 40 exports.

raw.assessment: The baseline misses both course-set and handling-time targets. Assignment changes and renames are associated with affected exports, but their causal roles are unproven. No sampled cross-center rows establishes neither isolation for course splits nor future safety. A bounded investigation should distinguish export membership errors from coordinator interpretation and import work.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for historical weeks may change which courses enter an export, even when that week's attendance has not changed.
openings.delta: Test week-specific course membership keyed by stable course identity and center, instead of assuming the present assignment represents the requested week.
openings.prediction: With historical attendance fixed, changing only the current assignment changes exported course membership under the incumbent; a correct week-specific rule keeps it invariant.
openings.probe: In staging, replay fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split-course fixtures against coordinator-confirmed weekly expectations. Compare course IDs internally and validate final CSVs, including center isolation and concurrent attendance entry. Estimate the smallest supported fix before committing the six-day budget.
assumptions: Stable identities and sufficiently complete assignment history exist or can be recovered within six engineer-days and current hosting costs.
Coordinators can specify intended membership for split and reassigned courses.

openings.claim: How much handling comes from genuinely missing courses, name-based reconciliation of present courses, or importing an otherwise correct CSV?
openings.delta: Separate file correctness from work performed after download; completion logs and replacement delays do not measure those activities.
openings.prediction: Name reconciliation produces false absence reports for complete renamed-course files; import friction produces long import segments even when course identities and names agree.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' sessions to compare fabricated, schema-valid unchanged, renamed-but-complete and truly incomplete files in counterbalanced order. Record correctness judgments and minutes spent checking, correcting, downloading and importing, separately from waiting.
assumptions: Fabricated schedules approximate ordinary reconciliation tasks.
Sessions and observations remain inside authorized workspaces and the existing private service.

openings.claim: Current assignments or mutable names may distort historical membership; splits need lineage rules.
openings.discriminator: With attendance fixed, assignment/name changes incorrectly alter selected course IDs, distinct from D2 false absence judgments.
openings.fit: Uncertain history and cost; preserve private names, documented CSV, concurrent entry and hosting allowance.
openings.probe: Compare incumbent and week-relevant stable-identity selectors on fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split fixtures with coordinator-confirmed expectations. Check another center, final CSV and concurrent entry; estimate feasibility.
openings.uncertainty: Association is not causation. Recoverable history/identity and split expectations are unverified; sampled isolation excludes the split-course center.

openings.claim: Handling may arise from real omissions, name reconciliation, imports or replacement requests.
openings.discriminator: Complete renamed files trigger false absence judgments; incomplete files require correction; correct stable files still incur import work.
openings.fit: Private authorized workspaces and schema-valid files; both probes share six engineer-days and existing hosting.
openings.probe: Counterbalance fabricated stable, renamed-complete and incomplete files across six coordinators’ two sessions. Record judgments; separately time checking, correcting, downloading, importing and requests, separating waiting.
openings.uncertainty: Timetable completeness/timing and task realism remain unmeasured; confirm session findings in actual exports.

lineage.reason: With A1; preserves names and splits.
With Z1; preserves fixed-attendance comparison and center identity.
With A2; preserves request effort versus waiting.
With Z2; preserves false absence, omissions and imports.

post_distill.decision: Probe before changing scheduling or capacity; stable-course handling already meets target. Verify next 40 exports: median ≤12 minutes, ≥95% intended sets, zero cross-center records. Synthetic evidence supports hypotheses only.
